newsitem.title: USA: U.S. refiners to keep autumn shutdowns light.
newsitem.headline: U.S. refiners to keep autumn shutdowns light.

text.p: The net loss of U.S. crude runs this fall quarter will be lighter than previous years as refiners battle to increase low stocks of heating oil winter fuel, analysts and traders said.
Experts estimated that runs would dip to only around a low of 14 million barrels per day (bpd), compared with the typical bottom of 13.8 million bpd near late October.
"I don't expect to see more than 500,000 barrels per day. It's most certainly due to the distillates (low stocks)," said Ken Miller, senior principal at Houston's Purvin & Gertz.
"Some historical records could be set at these times," Miller added, noting crude input to distillation was now 14.72 million bpd against 14.5 million bpd last year.
Current indications from refiners also pointed to a milder turnaround season, and an emphasis on maximizing heating oil and jet fuel, the latter spurred along by military demand.

"Refiners may try to make runs a little more moderate than required because they're in a real need to put heating oil in the tank," Charles McSpadden, vice president of market analysis at Bonner & Moore said, but noted there was pent up need for taking turnarounds due to recently high runs.
Last autumn saw significant turnaround volumes, with a peak of 14.8 million bpd established in early September and a low of 13.5 million bpd in October.
This year, refiners are more likely to maintain steady throughputs until the end of October.

"Just-in-time stocks are good financial policy, but refiners have to be concerned about public relations. Heating oil is not a luxury item," McSpadden said, referring to a rise in consumer costs with heating oil at five-year highs.
Upcoming refinery turnarounds include Sun Oil, Amerada Hess, and Conoco.
Sun will be taking down an 85,000 bpd cat cracker at its Marcus Hook, Pa. refinery from Oct 4 for 44-days of maintenance. Other related units will also undergo some work at the 175,000 bpd refinery.
Traders said Conoco's schedule includes shutting a 20,000 bpd cat cracker for two to three weeks mid October at its 160,000 bpd Ponca City, Okla. refinery.
Amerada Hess plans to expand a cat cracker at its St Croix, Virgin Islands refinery, taking the unit down for up to six weeks beginning this month.
